cells.tense: Right now the turning and the one standing in it are the same thing.
cells.act: close the cycle and leave the door open for the next
cells.ask: Finish the last small step of something basically done, then leave a way back in — a saved place, an open note — so the close stays open.
cells.core:
What's arriving, you meet as it comes. Nothing has to be held back for later and nothing has to be locked down once it's here — each moment lands and you're standing there to receive it. That isn't a trick you're performing. It's how this runs when it isn't being pushed, and it shows in how cleanly one thing can finish while the next is still unknown.

There is a piece of work, or a small routine, sitting at its last step. Close it — the actual final move, not one more pass of preparation. Then keep some way back in: a note, a saved file, an open invitation. Finishing it that way says something a clean cut wouldn't, that the end of a cycle and the start of the next can both be true of the same hour.
cells.sheetLine: You meet what arrives, and you can let it finish without sealing it.
cells.verb: meeting what is arriving, exactly as it arrives
cells.place: seeing the whole pattern from where you stand inside it

cells.tense: You are already living in a stretch of time that hasn't arrived yet.
cells.act: gather what it became and set it down whole
cells.ask: Pull the unfinished chase into one page — everything it actually turned into — and put the whole of it somewhere it can stay at that size.
cells.core:
Bracing for a future you can't write is doing the writing for you. When the next stretch hasn't landed, this starts rehearsing it — planning the arrival before it comes, treating timing as a problem to get ahead of. The pattern repeats in its own loop and carries you with it. From inside that, the cause keeps looking like it sits somewhere ahead.

The loop is a finished thing wearing a current label. Go back to what it turned into, put that in one place — a page, a list, the whole of it — and keep it at the size it actually reached. Finished means finished at that size, not stretched further to keep the chase going. Once it is all in one place, you're meeting it instead of running in front of it. That has a cost: the forward-pull goes quiet, and the quiet sits there unfilled.

cells.tense: Something has already closed and you are still holding its position open.
cells.act: let the finished thing be the start of something
cells.ask: Name a finished thing you've kept out of play and take the smallest first step it could feed — nothing planned after.
cells.core:
There's a threshold you keep standing at, and the crossing is already behind you. Keeping things not-quite-manifested, not-quite-released feels like holding a fixed position, and the stillness reads as something achieved. Meanwhile the turning happens just outside the frame, and you're watching from a step back.

What's wanted here is ending something cleanly. A cycle, a role, a version of a project kept in a hallway so the label doesn't get applied — name one, and pick the least that could follow from it. A next start, not a new plan. Take the first step of that. Letting a closed thing start something is how the threshold ends up behind you.

cells.tense: The turn is being made by something other than the one making it.
cells.act: set a direction and take the first step in it
cells.ask: Hold one direction for this week and take its first step — chosen from what's here now, not from how this usually goes.
cells.core:
Things keep arriving, and afterward they get explained. A consequence shows up and comes as a surprise; the turning keeps happening, and the turning isn't being claimed by anyone in particular. The direction is being set by the pattern rather than by the one standing in the middle of it, so arrivals come as things that happen to you rather than things you met.

Choosing is the way back, and it's plainer than it sounds. Hold one direction for this week, and take the first step in it — picked from what's here now, not from how this usually goes. You don't have to know why the pattern has held. You only have to make the turn on purpose and walk toward what you picked.
cells.sheetLine: The turn is happening without you claiming it — start claiming it.
